intro_line: A tiny British outpost where the Rock meets Mediterranean light.
intro: Gibraltar packs the Upper Rock, wild macaques and old fortifications into under 7 km², rewarding every slow walk with new views. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: Gibraltar has no metro or tram. The local currency is the Gibraltar pound (£, GBP), not USD.
Citibus (routes 5 and 10) and Gibraltar Bus Company (other routes) run the buses. Single fares start at £1.00 to £1.80.
Bus fares are flat, so distance does not change the price. Gibraltar Bus needs exact change or card; Citibus takes cash only.
Taxis are the easiest way up the steep roads. Check locally for ride-app coverage, as Uber is not reliably available.
Driving is on the right. Much of the old centre has narrow, one-way streets and very limited parking, so park in La Línea and walk across the border.
Walking covers most of the town. A cable car links the town with the Upper Rock, and a cruise port sits at the western end of Waterport Road.
